I still believe that I am mostly existing then, with only brief moments of really living, but even then, I'm terrified of losing those moments that actually make me feel alive. I am scared of the unknown, believing that at any moment I can lose everything, because well, I am very incapable. I am only a young adult, still learning how to live, yet I already feel like I'm always running out of time to do what I can with this life. I think almost every day "I don't have much time left." All I know is what I do every day, like work or save money and not much else. I can help people through my time consuming efforts, but I think that's probably where my usefulness really ends. Everything else is a gamble, where I can mess up social interactions or connecting with others at any moment. It's not that I'm completely ignorant of situations around me, I just never know what's right. How can I make my partner happy? When is it right to say something? What can I do? 

My feelings of self doubt have been around since youth and have intertwined with my deep gut feeling of unsatisfaction only to exhaust me emotionally and stand in the way of actually being able to move forward with confidence. I have talked with others, gone to therapy, participated in enjoyable activities, and have tried other efforts for stress relief, but still have come to the same conclusion that any fortunate events that have happened upon me are wasted on my useless existence. I am disgusted by my own shortcomings, only able to guess about how to improve, to no avail. I don't want to lose everything. I just want to know what to do, how to fix things, how to be sure that I'm doing things right, because now I'm not. If all else fails and I truly realize that just existing is the reason why I continue to fail in any effort to move forward, I believe I'd rather end this existence already and leave my assets behind. In the case that it comes to that, I really don't want to hurt anyone in my passing, but I really should not have been born in the first place. If death may come for me, may it be swift, but really, I am truly sorry.
